title: Microsoft Entra: cross-tenant synchronisation of security groups
summary: Hold: both target-tenant checkbox paths omit the link that opens inbound access settings. The claim that role-enabled group synchronization has no automation is also incorrect: Microsoft documents a corresponding Microsoft Graph PowerShell parameter. The roadmap facts, group provisioning default and source-tenant licensing are supported.

claims.claim: Cross-tenant synchronization can create security groups in another Microsoft Entra tenant.
claims.quote: Yes, cross-tenant synchronization can create security groups in the target tenant.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Group provisioning is admin-opt-in because the source group's Enabled mapping toggle defaults to No.
claims.quote: If you want to synchronize groups, set the Enabled toggle to Yes. By default, this toggle is set to No.

claims.claim: Group synchronization requires Entra ID Governance or Entra Suite licensing per synchronized user in the source tenant.

claims.quote: Role-enabled group sync synchronizes the group's ability to receive role assignments. It doesn't copy role assignments from the source tenant. Assign the required roles separately in each target tenant.

claims.quote: On the Provisioning page, under the Mappings section, select Provision Microsoft Entra ID Groups to open the Attribute Mapping page. If you want to synchronize groups, set the Enabled toggle to Yes.
claims.fix: Add the page heading before the toggle: 'Entra ID > Cross-tenant synchronization > Configurations > configuration > Provisioning > Mappings > Provision Microsoft Entra ID Groups > Attribute Mapping > Enabled'. The cited configure page opens Attribute Mapping after selecting the group mapping.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: A target security group can be granted access to SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: Security groups are used for granting access to Microsoft 365 resources, such as SharePoint sites. They can make administration easier because you need only administer the group rather than adding users to each resource individually.
claims.fix: Add 'Compare types of groups in Microsoft 365' at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/create-groups/compare-groups?view=o365-worldwide to sources for the SharePoint access example.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure and Security & identity
claims.claim: Members inherit permissions assigned to a group, so synchronizing membership transfers source membership decisions to target resource access.
claims.quote:
You can use Microsoft Entra security groups and Microsoft 365 Groups as the basis for securing access to resources.
Group owners – manage group settings and its membership
Members – inherit permissions and access assigned to the group
claims.fix: Add 'Secure external access with groups in Microsoft Entra ID and Microsoft 365' at https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/architecture/4-secure-access-groups to sources for group-based permission inheritance.

claims.claim: Subsequent provisioning cycles occur approximately every 40 minutes while the provisioning service runs.
claims.quote: The initial cycle takes longer to perform than subsequent cycles, which occur approximately every 40 minutes as long as the Microsoft Entra provisioning service is running.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Target-only group edits persist until a group change in the source causes them to be overridden.
claims.quote: Changes to the group in the target tenant aren't overridden automatically. They're overridden only if there's a change to the group in the source tenant.

claims.claim: Increasing object and membership volumes can lengthen synchronization cycles.
claims.quote: As the overall volume of objects and references increases, the time required to evaluate and synchronize changes can also increase. In environments with high scale, this can result in longer synchronization cycles and increased latency for updates to be reflected in the target tenant.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends scoping synchronization to necessary objects and relationships for performance.
claims.quote: To optimize performance, scope synchronization to only the users, groups, and relationships that are necessary.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Same-cloud user synchronization requires P1 licenses in the source tenant.

claims.claim: Using groups solely to scope user synchronization, without synchronizing group objects, requires P1.
claims.quote: Using groups only to determine which users are synchronized, without synchronizing the groups themselves, requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 licenses.

claims.claim: Tenants that enable External ID billing and provision external guests might incur External ID charges.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter and caps
claims.claim: For workforce B2B synchronization, External ID billing concerns guests rather than organizational members and requires billing subscription linkage.

For B2B collaboration, the MAU billing model applies only to external users who have a UserType value of Guest. It doesn't apply to users who originate from within the organization and have a UserType value of Member.

claims.claim: Synchronizing group objects across Microsoft cloud environments is unsupported.

claims.quote:

claims.claim: Setting inbound group synchronization false stops current synchronization without affecting groups already synchronized.
claims.quote: false causes any current group synchronization from the source tenant to the target tenant to stop. This property has no impact on existing groups that have already been synchronized.
